transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Um… I guess my work kind of pushed me to come in. I’m a waitress, and I’ve been having these moments during service where I just sort of… freeze. Not in a dramatic way, I don’t think, but enough that people noticed.

Like, I’d be standing by the soda station holding the cash drawer key, and instead of closing out checks I’d be repeating table numbers to myself or doing things in the wrong order. It scared my coworkers, I think. I’m not trying to cause problems or anything—I just… I don’t know why I keep getting stuck like that.
When you freeze like that, do you suddenly feel intense fear or panic?

I don’t think it’s panic, exactly. I mean, I get embarrassed after because people are looking at me, but in the moment it’s more like I just… blank out or get stuck. I’m not suddenly terrified, if that makes sense.
After one of these episodes, do you remember clearly what happened during it?

Mostly, yes… I mean, it’s not like I completely black out. I can remember pieces pretty clearly afterward, which is part of why it’s embarrassing.

Like I remember standing by the soda station with the cash drawer key in my hand, and I was supposed to be closing checks, but instead I was just repeating table numbers to myself. Or I’d do things in the wrong order and not really… switch back right away. It sounds worse when I say it out loud, sorry. But I do remember enough to know why everyone got worried.
During these episodes, do you feel unreal or like the world around you isn’t real?

I… don’t think so? Not like the whole room feels fake or anything. I’m usually still aware I’m at work and people are around.

It’s more that I get kind of stuck or foggy, maybe. But if you mean like everything seems unreal, I haven’t really noticed that. I hope that answers it okay.
Do these freezing episodes tend to happen when something reminds you of a very stressful or upsetting experience?

I don’t think it’s usually tied to, like, a memory or something upsetting. At least I haven’t noticed that.

It was more… what scared everyone at work was me freezing up in the middle of service, or doing things out of order. Like I’d be standing by the soda station holding the cash drawer key, and instead of closing checks I’d just be repeating table numbers to myself. It wasn’t because something reminded me of anything, I don’t think… I just sort of got stuck. Does that make sense?
Have there been times when you realized you couldn’t account for a chunk of time?

I don’t think so… not like I suddenly “come to” and hours are missing or anything.

Sometimes I lose track a little, like anyone does when things are busy or I’m embarrassed after, but I can usually piece together what happened. If there are gaps, they’re small enough that I haven’t really noticed them as chunks of time. Is that what you mean?
During these episodes, do you have trouble focusing on what people are saying to you?

Yeah… I think so, sometimes. I mean, I don’t want to make it sound like I’m ignoring people on purpose, because I’m not.

At work, when it happens, someone might be telling me what to do next and I just… don’t really take it in right. That’s when I freeze up or do things in the wrong order, like I’ll be standing by the soda station with the cash drawer key and repeating table numbers to myself instead of closing checks. People were trying to get my attention, and I guess I wasn’t really focusing on them the way I should have.

Does that make sense?
During these episodes, do you become confused about where you are or what’s going on around you?

I don’t think I forget where I am, exactly. Like, I know I’m at work, I know I’m in the restaurant.

It’s more that what’s going on around me gets… scrambled, maybe? Like during service, I’ll freeze up or do things out of order. I might be by the soda station holding the cash drawer key, and instead of closing checks I’m just repeating table numbers to myself. So I’m not lost about the place, but I guess I’m not really following what’s happening the way I’m supposed to.

I don’t know if that counts as confused. Does that answer it okay?
Do these freezing episodes usually happen when you’re feeling especially stressed or under pressure?

Yeah… I think it mostly happens when things are really busy, like during service when everyone needs something at once.

I don’t want to make it sound dramatic, but that’s when people at work got scared, I guess. I’d sort of freeze in the middle of everything, or do things in the wrong order — like standing by the soda station holding the cash drawer key and repeating table numbers to myself instead of closing checks.

So… yes, I think pressure makes it worse. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Outside of these episodes at work, do you worry excessively about a lot of different things?

Um… I don’t know. I mean, I worry about normal stuff, I guess — work, bills, whether people are upset with me — but I’m not sure I’d call it excessive.

It’s not like I’m sitting around worrying about everything all the time, at least I don’t think so. Maybe I get tense, but… I don’t want to overstate it.

Is that what you mean by a lot of different things?
When you freeze like that, are you unable to make yourself move or respond even though you’re aware of what’s happening around you?

I think… maybe partly? I’m aware enough to know I’m at work and that people are waiting on me, but in the moment I sort of get stuck.

Like, what scared everyone was that I’d freeze in the middle of service or do things out of order. I’d be standing by the soda station with the cash drawer key, and instead of closing checks I’d just be repeating table numbers to myself.

It’s embarrassing to say it like that. I’m not trying to ignore people, I just… don’t seem to move on to the next thing right then. Is that what you mean?
When this happens, can you still answer someone if they speak to you?

Sometimes, yeah… if someone says my name really directly, I can usually say something, but it might not make a lot of sense or it takes me a second.

What scared people at work was more that I’d be kind of stuck in the middle of service, or doing the wrong thing — like standing by the soda station holding the cash drawer key and just repeating table numbers instead of closing checks. I wasn’t trying to ignore anyone. I just… wasn’t getting to the next step right then.

I’m sorry, is that answering what you’re asking?
When you freeze, do you find yourself repeating the same words or actions over and over without meaning to?

Yeah… I guess that part does happen, a little.

I don’t mean to do it, but when I freeze at work I can get stuck repeating table numbers to myself, or just doing the wrong step over and over in my head. Like I said, I was standing by the soda station holding the cash drawer key, and instead of closing out checks I kept going over table numbers.

It sounds worse when I say it out loud. I’m not trying to be difficult or anything — I just kind of… get stuck there. Does that count as repeating?
When you get stuck repeating the table numbers, does it feel like you have to do it to make the feeling go away or to prevent something bad from happening?

I don’t think so… not like, “If I don’t say table 12 something bad will happen.” It’s not that clear in my head.

It’s more like I’m stuck on it, like my brain won’t move to the next step for a second. I’m not doing it on purpose, but I also don’t know if I’d say it makes a feeling go away. I’m sorry, I know that’s probably not a very exact answer.
Before these freezing episodes started, had you gone through something very frightening or overwhelming?

I don’t think there was one big thing, no. Not that I can point to and say, “after that, it started.”

I mean… work can be stressful, and I get overwhelmed sometimes, but I don’t want to make it sound like there was some horrible event if there wasn’t. I haven’t really noticed a specific frightening thing before the freezing episodes.

Is that what you mean?
During these freezing episodes, does it feel like you go into a trance?

I don’t know if I’d call it a trance exactly… maybe it looks that way from the outside.

At work, what scared everyone was that I’d just sort of freeze in the middle of service, or do things out of order. Like I was standing by the soda station holding the cash drawer key, and instead of closing checks I was just repeating table numbers. I wasn’t trying to be weird or ignore people — it was more like I got stuck and couldn’t shift to the next thing for a bit.

Does that count as a trance, or is that different?
Did these freezing episodes start around the time something in your life became especially stressful?

Maybe… yes, I think that’s probably fair to say.

It wasn’t like one sudden crisis, but this whole change in me has been building for about a year and a couple months, I guess. Around when they asked me to start taking on the evening shift lead responsibilities at the restaurant.

I don’t want to blame the job or make it sound dramatic, because I was trying to handle it, but that is around when things started feeling different. Does that answer what you’re asking?
Do these freezing episodes happen only when you’re under pressure at work, or do they also happen when you’re calm?

Mostly it’s happened when I’m under pressure at work, I think… like in the middle of service when everything is moving fast.

I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is, but that’s what scared people there — I’d kind of freeze up or do things out of order. Like that time by the soda station, I was holding the cash drawer key and repeating table numbers instead of closing checks.

When I’m calm, I don’t notice it as much… or at least it doesn’t stand out the same way. Is that helpful?
Outside of those work episodes, do you ever feel detached from yourself, like you’re watching yourself from the outside?

I don’t think so… not in that exact way.

I mean, I can get kind of overwhelmed or spaced out, maybe, but I wouldn’t say I feel like I’m floating above myself watching it happen. At least I haven’t really noticed that. Maybe I’m not describing it right, though. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
When you freeze like that, does everything around you fade into the background?

Kind of… I’m not sure if I’d say everything fades out exactly.

It’s more like I get stuck, and people are talking or waiting, and I’m not doing the next right thing. Like the thing that really scared everyone was when I was standing by the soda station with the cash drawer key in my hand, and instead of closing checks I was just repeating table numbers.

I know that sounds bad. I don’t mean I’m totally gone or anything… I just sort of freeze and lose the order of what I’m supposed to be doing. Is that what you mean?

target_item.manifestation: This whole change in me has been building for about a year and two months, since I was asked to take on the evening shift lead responsibilities.
target_item.reason: The question asks about when the freezing episodes began in relation to a stressful life change; the duration profile covers the timing of the overall change beginning after being asked to take on evening shift lead responsibilities.

patient.answer:
Maybe… yes, I think that’s probably fair to say.

It wasn’t like one sudden crisis, but this whole change in me has been building for about a year and a couple months, I guess. Around when they asked me to start taking on the evening shift lead responsibilities at the restaurant.

I don’t want to blame the job or make it sound dramatic, because I was trying to handle it, but that is around when things started feeling different. Does that answer what you’re asking?

inference.note: R41.0 is less likely because she remains oriented to place and situation, retains memory of episodes, and describes stress-related freezing/perseveration rather than global confusion. This turn further supports a stress-linked dissociative/functional presentation beginning after increased role pressure.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the episodes are specifically linked to stress, which best distinguishes an unspecified stress-related disorder from a dissociative trance/other dissociative presentation.
doctor.question: Do these freezing episodes happen only when you’re under pressure at work, or do they also happen when you’re calm?

target_item.name: Disorganized_Abnormal_Behavior
target_item.manifestation: What scared everyone at work is that I started freezing up in the middle of service or doing things out of order, like standing by the soda station holding the cash drawer key and repeating table numbers instead of closing checks.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about the context in which the freezing episodes occur, which directly relates to the described disorganized or abnormal behavior.

patient.answer:
Mostly it’s happened when I’m under pressure at work, I think… like in the middle of service when everything is moving fast.

I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is, but that’s what scared people there — I’d kind of freeze up or do things out of order. Like that time by the soda station, I was holding the cash drawer key and repeating table numbers instead of closing checks.

When I’m calm, I don’t notice it as much… or at least it doesn’t stand out the same way. Is that helpful?

doctor.intent: Determine whether there is a persistent depersonalization or derealization component, which would help distinguish other specified dissociative symptoms from a nonspecific stress-related condition.
doctor.question: Outside of those work episodes, do you ever feel detached from yourself, like you’re watching yourself from the outside?

target_item.reason: The question is about depersonalization or dissociation—feeling detached from oneself or watching oneself from outside—which is not covered by the provided symptom profile items.

patient.answer:
I don’t think so… not in that exact way.

I mean, I can get kind of overwhelmed or spaced out, maybe, but I wouldn’t say I feel like I’m floating above myself watching it happen. At least I haven’t really noticed that. Maybe I’m not describing it right, though. Is that the kind of thing you mean?

doctor.intent: Determine whether the episodes involve a narrowed, trance-like awareness of the surroundings, which would help distinguish a dissociative trance/conversion-type presentation from a nonspecific stress-related condition.
doctor.question: When you freeze like that, does everything around you fade into the background?

target_item.name: Disorganized_Abnormal_Behavior
target_item.manifestation: What scared everyone at work is that I started freezing up in the middle of service or doing things out of order, like standing by the soda station holding the cash drawer key and repeating table numbers instead of closing checks.
target_item.reason: The question is asking about what happens during the freezing episodes, which are part of the abnormal/disorganized behavior described in this profile.

patient.answer:
Kind of… I’m not sure if I’d say everything fades out exactly.

It’s more like I get stuck, and people are talking or waiting, and I’m not doing the next right thing. Like the thing that really scared everyone was when I was standing by the soda station with the cash drawer key in my hand, and instead of closing checks I was just repeating table numbers.

I know that sounds bad. I don’t mean I’m totally gone or anything… I just sort of freeze and lose the order of what I’m supposed to be doing. Is that what you mean?

opening_question.intent: Identify the patient's chief concern and reason for seeking psychiatric care today
opening_question.question: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

final_diagnosis.reason: The episodes are most consistently linked to identifiable psychosocial stress/pressure at work, began around increased job responsibilities, and involve transient freezing, impaired attention, and repetitive behavior without clear evidence of panic, trauma-related re-experiencing, major dissociative amnesia, depersonalization/derealization, or compulsions. This fits a stress-related disorder best among the listed options, while dissociative trance/other dissociative phenomena remain a differential.
